concept.name: Chande momentum oscillator
concept.definition: Tushar Chande's momentum oscillator: 100 times the difference between summed up-moves and summed down-moves over n periods divided by their total, bounding raw, unsmoothed momentum between -100 and +100.
concept.intuition: It is a tug-of-war score between up days and down days: if all movement over the window was up, CMO is +100; all down, -100.
concept.mechanics: Sum the gains of up closes and the losses of down closes separately over n periods; CMO = 100 x (Su - Sd)/(Su + Sd). Readings beyond +/-50 are treated as overbought/oversold; divergences and zero-line crosses give trend signals.
concept.formula: CMO(n) = 100 x (Su - Sd) / (Su + Sd), where Su = sum of max(C_i - C_{i-1}, 0) and Sd = sum of max(C_{i-1} - C_i, 0) over n periods.
concept.failure_modes: Unsmoothed, so it is noisier than RSI and reaches its extremes more often; overbought/oversold levels fail in strong trends, as with all bounded oscillators.
concept.misconceptions: CMO is not a smoothed RSI - it nets raw sums rather than Wilder-smoothed average gains and losses, and the +/-50 thresholds are conventions, not validated cutoffs.
concept.example: Over 20 days with up-moves totaling 30 points and down-moves 10: CMO = 100 x (30-10)/(30+10) = +50.
